analysis.answer: Current law allows each county to decide whether to honor federal immigration detainer requests. The measure overrides this local discretion, prohibiting any county jail from holding an individual beyond their normal release time solely due to a federal detainer.

Immigrants subject to detainer requests benefit by avoiding extended detention in county jails. Federal immigration authorities bear an enforcement cost, as they lose the ability to have individuals held by local jails while arranging for custody transfers. Counties may save on local detention costs but lose flexibility.

Federal immigration authorities may have to deploy personnel to county jails prior to individuals' exact release times to take custody directly. Counties currently honoring these requests will have to change their jail release protocols.

The measure addresses the extended detention of immigrants in local facilities without local criminal justification, resolving it by forbidding holds based solely on federal detainers. From an opposing view, it creates an entry barrier for federal agents seeking to take custody of individuals from local jails.
The state gains power over detention policy at the expense of county governments and sheriffs, who lose the discretion to cooperate with federal detainer requests by extending local holds.
